requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation maps to marked code and to a test that exercises it.

**Obligations and code**
- **Command form** (`habeas author <full-name> [--config] [--missing|--force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`): `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` (the `Author` variant) defines the flags. `--missing` conflicts with `--force` and `--stdout`. `src/main.rs#fn[main]` dispatches to `habeas::authoring::author_evidence_with_options`.
- **Authoring one existing requirement or named example under `requirements.authoring.refresh`:**
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#enum[AuthoringSubject]` and `#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[parse]` parse the subject.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` rejects a name that is not a requirement or example (the "no matching requirement or named example" error).
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]` makes `--stdout` imply force and skips a current subject via `src/authoring/batch.rs#fn[subject_is_current]`. It does this before resolving configuration.
  - `#fn[configured_assessment]` and `#fn[configured_record]` resolve configuration and assess the subject.
- **Report of subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage path:**
  - `src/main.rs#fn[main]` prints `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"`, then `Evidence: <path>` and `Usage: <path>`.
  - `AuthoringOutcome` and `EvidenceOutput` carry these values.
- **Evidence destination is the file path by default and `stdout` under `--stdout`:** `configured_assessment` sets `evidence_path` to `Some(path)` for file output and `None` for stdout. `main` prints `Evidence: {path}` or `Evidence: stdout`.
- **Report and diagnostics go to stderr in stdout mode:**
  - `main` uses `eprintln!` for the stdout-mode report and for the false-determination note.
  - Coverage-loss reviews cannot run in stdout mode, because `configured_assessment` reads the replaced records only for file output. Their failures use `eprintln!`.
  - The only printing in `src/authoring` is `eprintln!` in `progress.rs`.
  - Errors returned from `main` go to stderr.
- **`author-evidence` alias:** `#[command(alias = "author-evidence", …)]` on `Command::Author`.

**Tests**
- **Default report:** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` runs `author-evidence`. It asserts stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`, that `Evidence:` ends with `evidence/SUBJECT.json` and resolves to the project file, and that `Usage:` is present.
- **Stdout mode:** `#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` checks stdout holds only the JSON. It checks stderr holds the subject/backend/model line, `Evidence: stdout`, `Usage:` and the false/FIXME notes. It also covers `--verbose`.
- **Verbose:** `#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` covers `-v` and `--verbose`.
- **Unknown subject and conflicting targets:** `#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]`.
- **Refresh behaviour:** `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` covers the following:
  - the default `--missing` keeps current records, and `--missing` given explicitly does the same;
  - `--missing` with `--force` and `--missing` with `--stdout` are rejected;
  - `--force` reassesses;
  - `--stdout` implies `--force`;
  - the alias works.
- **`--config`:** used in several tests, for example `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs`.

The `{test}` references on `Fixture`, `run` and `command` are helpers for these tests.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
